properties.description:
TWO defects from the StoryFlow fleet's 2026-08-15/16 log, both verified in source before the fix and both with the reporter's diagnosis CORRECTED. They ship together because they are one shape: a signal that could not express its own limit.

① A QUESTION NOT CREATED BY gap_to_prompt WAS PERMANENTLY UNANSWERABLE. `set_question_status` derived the Question id by string formatting from the gap id (`detect.rs:700-702`) and did a single `get_node`, so a hand-authored Question was unreachable — while `open_questions` published its `question_id` and `answer_question` refused to take one. The loop then reported 'follow it up rather than asking again' about something it structurally could not close, and the next seat re-asks the user what they already ruled on. FIX: `resolve_question_id` tries the DERIVED id first and the argument verbatim second, so every existing caller is byte-identical and the unreachable case becomes reachable; the MCP tool now accepts `gap_id` OR `question_id`; and the refusal names the ids that DO exist rather than only the miss — the round trip the reporter had no way to shortcut. `withdraw_question` shares the resolver and gains the same reach.

② `sync` REPORTED `in_step` WHILE THIS GRAPH HELD UNEXPORTED WORK. ⚠️ THE REPORTER'S DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG AND THE CORRECTION IS THE FINDING: they called it a measure-itself bug. The mechanism is exactly as they described — the cheap gate compares the file against the hash this graph last wrote it with (`sync_debt.rs:199`) and `bare()` hardcodes `nodes_not_here_total: 0` — but `ver:the-record-moved-is-surfaced` pins 'ordinary unexported work is NEVER reported' as the property the whole design rests on. The code is CORRECT. The defect is that NOTHING covered the other direction, and `in_step` in a field called `sync` was read as covering both. FIX: every sync entry now carries `live_nodes` beside `export_nodes`, and the in-step line says how many nodes have never been exported. It changes no state and no verdict — unexported work is still not `behind`, because that would tell a session to import over its own unsaved work.

MEASURED, AND THE REPRODUCTION IS WHY ② IS RECORDED RATHER THAN FILED: at the start of the session that fixed it, `loop_status.sync` reported `in_step` with `nodes_not_here_total: 0` for reflow2's OWN export while two TemporalFacts sat live and absent from it — an earlier session's entire triage of music_graph F23 and F24. The previous handoff had recorded 'nothing behind' on the strength of that green. They survived only because this session exported for an unrelated reason.

MUTATION-CHECKED THREE WAYS, each killing exactly the test that names it and no other: dropping the verbatim fallback fails the hand-authored and withdraw cases only; swapping the resolver order so the verbatim id wins fails ONLY the collision counterweight, which is the case proving a widened lookup did not become a guessing one; and firing the unexported warning on `live >= export` instead of `>` fails ONLY the fully-exported counterweight, which is what stops a reading aid becoming a false alarm on the path every ordinary session takes.

THE SERVED SURFACE CHANGED, deliberately and only by WIDENING: `answer_question.gap_id` leaves the required list and `question_id` joins the schema, so no existing caller breaks. Toolsnap regenerated (149).

BOUNDS, stated rather than discovered later: the sync counts are NODES ONLY — counting edges means walking every node's adjacency, which costs what the export costs, and paying that on the ordinary path is the one thing this check exists to avoid, so an edge-only divergence stays invisible. They are counts, not ids, so equal counts with different ids still pass: this is a reading aid, never a durability guarantee. And neither fix addresses why an ANSWERED question still does not become design — reflow2's own loop has carried '1 answered question never reached the design' for days, and that gap is real independently of the id scheme.
properties.name: A question is answerable by either id, and an in-step record says how much of this graph it does not hold — two signals that could not previously be wrong out loud
